title: Pick the adapter with a 24/29 cone and seat it in a 24/29 socket
instruction: pick the adapter with the 24/29 cone and seat it in the 24/29 socket
context: Assembling lab apparatus means picking the adapter whose joint matches by size, from a rack of similar-looking ones. A smaller cone still drops into the socket but leaves a loose, leaking joint, so 'it goes in' is not enough. Done by: chemical technicians and laboratory chemists.
setup: Positions in metres on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 and -0.305. Every adapter, including the fixed one, is white PTFE plastic. Fixed: a dark grey clamp block (painted aluminium or wood) 50 x 50 mm, 60 mm tall, centred at (0.30, 0.00), holding a plastic expansion adapter with its 24/29 socket facing up; in the simulation the socket is a square bore 27 mm across and 29 mm deep with 5 mm walls, its floor the block's top, its rim 89 mm above the table. Loose: four plastic expansion adapters in a row across the table at x = 0.17, each standing upright on its cone inside a fixed grey plastic collar (square, 4 mm wider inside than the cone, 4 mm walls, 20 mm tall). Each adapter is a cone at the bottom, an 18 mm by 15 mm neck, and a socket at the top (6 mm wider outside than its joint size): at y = 0.15 a 29/32 cone to 34/35 socket (60 g, 82 mm tall); at y = 0.05 a 14/23 cone to 19/26 socket (30 g, 64 mm tall); at y = -0.05 a 24/29 cone to 29/32 socket (45 g, 76 mm tall); at y = -0.15 a 19/26 cone to 29/32 socket (40 g, 73 mm tall). Joint sizes are moulded on each adapter, as on real ones. Only the adapter at y = -0.05 has a 24/29 cone, and every upper end is a socket. All parts share one friction (0.4). Both arms start at their ready poses.
scoring: End state, judged after the arms let go, from a side photo and a ruler. Gate: 0 if any adapter other than the 24/29 one is down in the socket (the centre of its cone's lower end more than 2 mm below the rim and inside the bore seen from above); only the 14/23 and 19/26 cones can get there, and the 29/32 cone is too wide to enter. Otherwise: 1.0 if the 24/29 adapter is seated (the centre of its cone's lower end within 3 mm of the socket floor and within 3 mm of the socket's axis, and the adapter within 4 degrees of vertical), held for 1 s; 0.5 if its cone's lower end is at least 10 mm below the rim, inside the bore and within 20 degrees of vertical, but not seated; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the four adapters back in their collars in the same order. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Approximate. Tapered cones are straight cylinders and the round socket is a square bore with 1.5 mm of play, so the 14/23 and 19/26 cones drop to the socket floor where real ones would sit loose; both score 0. Upper sockets are solid. Moulded joint sizes can't be read at 320 x 176, so in simulation adapters are told apart by size. Masses are close to solid PTFE parts. One friction (0.4) for every contact.
